another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm responsible for one child - my son Alex. He's 15 years old and lives with me here at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Are you currently the one claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else (such as another parent or guardian) already claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that. A few more questions:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training? For example, is he attending school?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's at school - he's doing his GCSEs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's focused on his schoolwork. And he's not claiming any benefits himself either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question:

**Do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a British citizen, or do you have any other immigration status I should be aware of? Or is this not applicable to your situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, so that shouldn't be an issue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✅ Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
✅ You live with Alex in the UK and are responsible for him
✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✅ Alex is in approved education (studying for his GCSEs at school)
✅ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
✅ Alex is not claiming benefits in his own right
✅ You are a British citizen living in the UK

All the eligibility criteria are met, so you should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**What to do next:**
You can apply for Child Benefit if you haven't already done so. 

**Important to note:**
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge
- Child Benefit will normally continue until Alex turns 16, and can continue until he's 20 if he stays in approved education or training

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
